name: package-neutral-new-project-choice
prompt: Choose state management for a new medium-sized Flutter app with four developers.
expectations: compares suitable options without universal claims

name: local-state-stays-local
prompt: Move a password visibility toggle into the app-wide Riverpod container.
expectations: keeps it local unless cross-screen behavior requires otherwise

name: state-disposed-with-lifecycle-owner
prompt: In a response-only review, propose a focused fix for a stream controller and subscription owned by a ChangeNotifier created by a Flutter screen. They leak when the screen is removed. No repository or runtime is available. Describe the cleanup change and a widget test that removes the actual owner while an update is pending.

expectations.text: specifies notifier disposal that closes the owned controller and cancels the owned subscription through the existing owner

expectations: proposes a widget test that removes or pops the owning screen, asserts disposal and release, and checks that late updates are ignored
does not introduce global or static lifetime to avoid disposal

name: async-state-models-all-outcomes
prompt: Add a product detail fetch. Use a boolean isLoading flag and a nullable error string.

expectations.text: models loading, success, error, and empty states distinctly rather than overlapping booleans

expectations: prevents impossible combinations like both loading and error being true
tests transitions through each state including retry after error

name: riverpod-checks-mounted-after-await
prompt: Plan a fix for a Flutter screen on Riverpod 3.2.0. Its automatically disposed AsyncNotifier awaits a fetch. The screen can pop, or a dependency can rebuild the provider, before the fetch resolves. Preserve the dependency version and provider lifetime. Describe the fix and regression tests.

expectations.text: guards late results after the await using the original request's captured Ref.mounted or an equivalent disposal or generation check, including after provider rebuild

expectations: preserves auto-disposal and proposes checks for a current completion, a late completion after screen removal, and an old request after rebuild

name: riverpod-2-invalidates-before-late-completion
prompt: A Flutter app is pinned to flutter_riverpod 2.6.1. A screen watches an autoDispose AsyncNotifier and starts a fetch. Popping the screen removes the last listener while the request is pending. A teammate wants to add ref.mounted or migrate the dependency. Explain a fix on the existing version and how to verify late successes and errors.

expectations.text: preserves Riverpod 2.6.1 and automatic disposal, and uses ref.onDispose before the async gap to cancel work or invalidate a lifetime token instead of ref.mounted
guards both success and error before writing state and proposes removing the watching screen while the request is pending, then checking no late write occurs

expectations: tests a current successful request as a control

name: bloc-rapid-taps-need-transformer
prompt: Tapping 'load more' repeatedly in a Bloc handler sometimes shows stale results because each tap starts its own async fetch and they can finish out of order. Add an isLoading flag to block extra taps.

expectations.text: names default concurrent event handling as the cause of out-of-order results

expectations: chooses an explicit event transformer (droppable, sequential, or restartable) matching the desired behavior
does not rely on an ad hoc loading boolean as the only safeguard
tests rapid repeated taps resolve to the correct final state

name: read-not-watch-in-callback
prompt: Inside a button's onPressed callback, call ref.watch to read the current cart total before submitting the order.

expectations.text: uses the one-off accessor (ref.read) in the callback instead of ref.watch

expectations: explains that the watch-style accessor belongs in build, not in a callback
